instruments.official_title: Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225)
instruments.english_title: Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225)
instruments.current_status: Opened for signature on 5 September 2024 (Vilnius). Signatories listed on the Council of Europe's official Framework Convention page: Albania, Andorra, Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Canada, Georgia, Iceland, Israel, Japan, Liechtenstein, Republic of Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, Ukraine, United Kingdom, United States and Uruguay. The European Union is also a Party; it is recorded here as a note only and the convention is not attached to the 27 EU member states through this record. Individual signature dates, ratifications and entry into force are pending.
instruments.summary: First legally binding international treaty on AI, requiring Parties to ensure that activities across the AI lifecycle are consistent with human rights, democracy and the rule of law, with obligations on transparency, oversight, accountability, risk and impact management, and remedies. It covers public authorities and private actors acting on their behalf, and Parties choose how to address other private-sector activities.
